 These Appeals, Coming On For Admission, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
1.
The insurer is in appeals challenging the compensation awarded for the injuries suffered by the claimant and also compensation awarded towards damages to the vehicle.
2. The principal contention of the insurer is that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a driving licence and the lorry did not have a permit.

3. In my view, since the insurer is essentially contending that there is a breach of a policy condition,
it would have to primarily pay the compensation and thereafter proceed to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
4. In that view of the matter, the direction of the Tribunal directing the insurer to deposit the compensation is affirmed.
However, the insurer is granted liberty to seek for recovery of the compensation paid after the compensation amount has been deposited before the Tribunal.
